title: Leaving the California for Hobbs, New Mexico, and the Ramona's racketeer owner
summary: After a year as MC with a new group, Watts goes to Hobbs and finds the Ramona nightclub controlled by oilman and slot-machine racketeer Cecil Thompson.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: I went to the California. Yeah. And played with these boys, Dinah, Dinah, Dinah, Joy had booked in there, see. But after you left there, where'd you went? Well, no. Went to New Mexico? Yeah. Went to Hobbs? Yeah, I worked there, oh yeah. I worked there for about a year though for a joint this time. Did you? Oh yeah. I was MC. When I went and took over the band, Tiny Joe was out. I see. See?
That's how Joe did MC'ing too, huh?

Yes, he did, and had one of the loveliest voice. Because he did the kids. Man, when he sing Cocktails for Two, that was popular in those years. And he couldn't set no chair, because he'd break all the chairs up. He'd just set right on the bandstand, just fall around, you know, on the bandstand, man. Oh, Mr. Five by Five, but he had a wonderful voice. That's true, though. Yeah. Well, I worked there, like I said, about a year. And then I hit on up in Hobbs, see? I went to Hobbs. That's New Mexico. Mm-hmm. And, well, this is a coincidence, because when I went to Hobbs, at the Ramona nightclub, they're playing for Cecil Thompson, he was a, man, I'm telling you, you don't have to go to Chicago at Enoges for gangsters. He was a big racketeer, man. He had a lot of, he had all the slot machines showed up, all of them down that part of Texas. And that's direct in the oil field, as you know Hobbs is. Yeah, Hobbs is basically. And he had his hands in oil. He had his hands in this. Anything crew that you want to go by, anything. Don't care what it was, call girls anything. You got to go through Caesar first. He's got to give it okay. And he was his own bouncer, and a little five, three-foot man. What? And I've seen him throw them big oil, man, would work on them rigs, man out there, them big six feet man, man, like there was nothing. What? He was just much power. He said he didn't need no bouncer. He was his bouncer. Oh, sure. And nobody met all them boys up there.
Yeah, they had that bad thing.
